items.title: Agents are sessions, not requests: size GKE node pools for AI agent sessions
items.summary: AI agent sessions remain active and idle for most of the workday, making traditional one-Pod-per-session allocations inefficient for cluster resources. By using open-source tools like Agent Substrate and AX on GKE, developers can park idle sessions in object storage to release compute resources while maintaining session state. This approach optimizes resource utilization and reduces Kubernetes node costs by up to 40%.

items.title: Distributed LLM Training Across Metros: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText
items.summary: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText enables developers to efficiently train large language models across geographically distributed TPU slices by streaming parameter fragments instead of synchronizing full models at every step. This approach slashes cross-slice communication volume by over 60× and eliminates network stalls, allowing seamless multi-datacenter scaling without degrading model convergence or quality.

items.title: On-Device Speech Recognition and Text-to-Speech in Google AI Edge Gallery
items.summary: Google AI Edge Gallery now supports on-device, offline Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) and Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities for building developer-friendly voice applications. Developers can leverage ML Kit for optimized Android performance, or use MediaPipe Tasks and LiteRT for cross-platform open-weight model integration. This local pipeline seamlessly pairs lightweight speech models with on-device small language models like Gemini Nano and Gemma 4 to enable real-time streaming transcription and low-latency synthesis.

items.title: Announcing Long-Context Training on TPUs with MaxText Context Parallelism
items.summary: Google Cloud's MaxText framework now supports long-context training up to 14 million tokens on Cloud TPUs by implementing four context-parallel strategies: All-gather, A2A, P2P, and USP. Powered by the Tokamax Splash Attention kernel, these strategies effectively manage attention compute and memory bottlenecks without materializing full key-value sequences in high-bandwidth memory. Developers can adopt these capabilities in MaxText v0.2.4 to achieve high Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) across large-scale model training workflows.

items.title: Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Tunix and Gemma 4 on Google TPUs
items.summary: This post walks developers through training a multi-turn, tool-using LLM agent using Tunix and Gemma 4 on Cloud TPUs. By leveraging agentic Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and asynchronous vLLM rollouts, the approach significantly improves complex reasoning and tool compliance in interactive environments.

items.title: Gemini 4 Hydrogen: a faster model for general purpose robotics
items.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings strong spatial and embodied reasoning capabilities to a fast, efficient model built specifically for robotics. To help developers put these capabilities to work, the new Robotics plugin for Google Antigravity transforms the platform into a comprehensive workbench supporting rapid hardware bring-up, MuJoCo simulation, and closed-loop control. Developers can leverage these tools to transition from an unboxed robot arm to a fully functional real-to-sim-to-real application in an afternoon using natural language prompts and day-one support in the google-genai SDKs.

items.title: A2UI 1.0: Build delightful, fast, reliable, agentic experiences
items.summary: A2UI 1.0 is an open protocol for generative UI that enables AI agents to render interactive, native screens across web, mobile, and desktop applications. Developers can leverage open-source renderer SDKs—including React, Angular, Lit, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose—alongside agent SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and Dart. The release introduces bidirectional function calls, swappable inference formats, and secure data binding to help teams seamlessly integrate generative UI into their product stacks.

items.title: Agent Distraction
items.summary: Analysis of over 913,000 coding agent sessions reveals that 13% expose agents to inline TODO(b/...) comments. In 6% of encounters, agents act on these comments, with 83% being entirely unprompted by the developer. These detours result in significant overhead—adding 70% more steps, 77% more tokens, and 105% more wait time per session—split between chasing closed tickets (41%) and unauthorized scope creep on open bugs (57%). Higher-capability models show higher distraction rates, highlighting the need for automated cleanup and linters to maintain agent-friendly codebases

items.title: TPU Model Design Considerations and Optimization Guide
items.summary: The newly launched AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-codesign guide provides hardware-grounded design rules to help developers maximize performance on TPUs for LLMs and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) workloads. Key principles include aligning reduction and output dimensions to 256 for systolic arrays, adopting LatentMoE to compress routed token traffic, and mapping parallel axes directly onto physical links.

items.title: What is Pathways? Single-controller training for large models
items.summary: Pathways is a single-controller distributed training system designed to coordinate large-scale model training across multiple accelerator groups by representing computations as a global dataflow graph. Unlike traditional SPMD models like DDP and FSDP that rely on synchronous collectives, Pathways uses asynchronous dispatch and a central scheduler to maximize hardware utilization and prevent deadlocks in complex workloads. By decoupling model definition from physical hardware via virtual devices, developers can efficiently scale complex training architectures and seamlessly handle dynamic workloads like reinforcement learning post-training.

items.title: How Agent Anomaly Detection scores on benchmarks we didn't write

Developers can integrate AAD alongside semantic governance and strict tool limits as part of a defense-in-depth strategy to secure agentic applications.

items.title: Financial Research Retrieval with Node.js: Privacy Controls and Citation Quality
items.summary: The hard part of a financial research dashboard is not choosing a vector database. It is deciding what an answer is allowed to see, how fresh that evidence must be, and how every sentence gets a citation. A retrieval contract makes those constraints explicit before an endpoint or SDK enters the design. Short answer: use durable vector retrieval for governed filings and notes, live web retrieval for changing context, and combine both only when the answer records which source supplied each claim. Write down the retrieval unit first. For a filing, that might be a section-sized chunk with issuer, fiscal_period, document_type, access_scope, and source_url metadata. A query should carry the viewer's allowed scope, a freshness budget, and the number of citations required. This turns “find relevant text” into a testable interface. Privacy controls belong at this boundary. Filter out restricted documents before generation, and keep the policy decision observable alongside the retrieved IDs. Do not rely on a prompt telling the model to ignore a private note; the model should never receive it. Ingestion, querying, and citation assembly are separate stages. items.title: I Built Filelayer Because Storing Files and Managing User Files Are Two Different Problems
items.summary: I benchmarked five approaches to implementing file infrastructure in a SaaS application. Three were executed and tested. The results were more interesting than I expected. Most SaaS applications eventually need to handle user files. At first, this looks like a storage problem. You need somewhere to upload files, store them and serve them back. But as the application grows, more requirements appear: Who owns each file? Which user or workspace can access it? How do permissions work? How do you share files securely? How do you handle expiration and deletion? How do you audit access? How do you prevent common security mistakes? I built Filelayer around this problem: the application layer between a SaaS product and its underlying storage. items.title: 3 Object Storage Controls for Signed Download URLs in SaaS Receipt Exports
items.summary: TL;DR: Keep each original receipt in private object storage, keep tenant ownership in the application database, and mint a short-lived download URL only after an authenticated request passes authorization. This is the simplest delivery path when an e-commerce customer or auditor needs a later download, not a permanent public address. Choose the provider by the control boundary you need: an aggregator reduces integration and credential work; a direct storage specialist gives you deeper storage controls. The separation is small. Your database decides who may receive a receipt. Object storage decides how the approved caller can fetch its bytes for a limited time. A signed URL is a temporary bearer credential, so its lifetime should match the download window rather than the retention period of the receipt. For teams already integrating several backend services, Infrai is worth trying for this signing boundary. They are small projects. But I care about them a lot. I found a method that works for me. I write the documentation of my own projects, and I publish it on my site. While I write, I read the code. Then I read it again. And again. When I have to explain a module in plain words, I suddenly see the strange parts: a method that does too much, a default that makes no sense, a case nobody tested. items.title: Sending Files Phone to PC Without an App: What WebRTC Can and Cannot Do
items.summary: Every time I want to move a photo from my phone to my laptop, I go through the same ritual: find a cable, plug it in, wonder why the laptop does not see the phone, then email the photo to myself. It works, but it feels like a workaround for a problem browser APIs solved years ago. Here is what I learned while looking into browser-based transfer tools, and why DropAny is a decent example of the pattern. WebRTC is usually associated with video calls, but RTCDataChannel is just a bidirectional pipe between two peers. For file transfer you need three things: Signaling. Two browsers that have never met need to exchange SDP offers and ICE candidates. That requires a tiny server, but the server only relays text — the files never touch it. A pairing step. Typing a long room ID on a phone keyboard is miserable, so most tools generate a short one-time code. DropAny uses a 6-digit code or a QR scan, which is single-use and expires after 10 minutes. items.title: vite: command not found? Run the local binary the right way
items.summary: First published on the VMHeaven blog: vite: command not found? Run the local binary the right way. The canonical points there; the full guide covers npm/pnpm/yarn, CI and global installs. Short answer: Vite is a local devDependency, not a global command. vite: command not found (or sh: vite: command not found) almost always means you ran plain vite in a shell where the project's local binary (node_modules/.bin) is not on PATH. Install dependencies, then run Vite through the tool that knows about node_modules/.bin: npm install npm run dev # uses the "dev": "vite" script in package.json Or run the local binary directly, without a script: npx vite pnpm and yarn have their own: pnpm install && pnpm dev # or: pnpm exec vite yarn install && yarn dev # or: yarn vite vite fails npm run dev works but vite does not - that is expected. npm scripts put node_modules/.bin on PATH; your interactive shell does not. items.title: I built a 2FA code generator where the key never leaves the browser
items.summary: Sometimes you have a 2FA secret key but not the phone: a new device, a shared team account, a test login. Most "online 2FA" sites solve this, but it's rarely clear whether your key is sent to their server. So I built Get2FA, a TOTP generator that runs 100% client-side. TOTP (RFC 6238) is simple: decode the Base32 secret, take the current 30-second counter, compute an HMAC and truncate it to 6 digits. Browsers already ship HMAC-SHA1/256/512 in the Web Crypto API, so no library is needed: const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', secretBytes, { name: 'HMAC', hash: 'SHA-1' }, false, ['sign']); const mac = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.sign('HMAC', key, counterBytes)); const o = mac[mac.length - 1] & 15; const code = (((mac[o] & 127) << 24) | (mac[o + 1] << 16) | (mac[o + 2] << 8) | mac[o + 3]) % 1e6; The whole engine is about 200 lines and is tested against the official RFC 4226 and RFC 6238 vectors. Bulk mode: paste many keys, or lines like login|password|SECRET, and copy all codes at once. Google Authenticator export: the export QR uses otpauth-migration:// with a protobuf payload. A tiny hand-written protobuf reader turns it back into normal keys. Private links: get2fa.

items.summary: Scheduled broken-link and redirect checks that tell you the moment a link breaks — linkbruno.com Open the console on almost any website and you'll eventually see it: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found) It's a broken link, just not one a human clicked. The page asked the browser to fetch something (a script, a stylesheet, an image, a font, a JSON file, a source map), the browser requested it, and the server said it doesn't exist. items.title: How to Convert Decimal to Binary by Hand (and Why 0.1 Never Ends)
items.summary: Converting decimal to binary comes down to one repeated move: divide by 2 and keep the remainder. Here is the method, a second mental shortcut, and the edge cases (fractions, negatives, language built-ins) that catch people out. Divide the number by 2 and write down the quotient and the remainder (always 0 or 1). Repeat with the quotient until it reaches 0. Then read the remainders from last to first. Take 156: Division Quotient Remainder 156 ÷ 2 78 0 78 ÷ 2 39 0 39 ÷ 2 19 1 19 ÷ 2 9 1 9 ÷ 2 4 1 4 ÷ 2 2 0 2 ÷ 2 1 0 1 ÷ 2 0 1 Read upward: 10011100. Check it by adding the places that hold a 1: 128 + 16 + 8 + 4 = 156. That is 8 bits, so it fits in one byte. Why it works: each division asks whether the number is odd or even. Odd means a 1 in the 1s place. The rest is halved, and the same question now covers the 2s place, then the 4s. Remainders come out smallest place first, which is why you read them back upward. Below 256 there is a faster mental route. List 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 and ask, left to right, whether each one fits into what is left. If it does, write 1 and subtract. If not, write 0. items.title: Node.js Browser Direct Storage Upload with 30-Day Presigned URL Retention
items.summary: Use a Node.js backend to issue a short-lived presigned URL for each browser direct storage upload, and keep retention state in your own database. The deciding constraint is deletion: a per-tenant game backup is only recoverable while both its object and its restore record exist. TL;DR: make the browser a byte mover, not the policy authority. The backend chooses a tenant-scoped key, records a 30-day deletion deadline, and issues a narrow upload URL. A worker later deletes expired objects and marks the matching records deleted. This design keeps application code replaceable across AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Supabase Storage, UploadThing, or a multi-vendor surface such as Infrai. The fragile version looks like this in words: browser chooses a bucket and permanent URL, browser uploads, UI stores that URL, and nobody owns expiry. A provider migration then reaches into database rows, frontend rendering, CORS policy, and cleanup jobs at once. The better version is short: browser asks your API for an upload grant; API returns a short-lived URL plus an application-level backup ID; browser uploads; API records completion; restore asks your API for a short-lived download grant. items.summary: TL;DR: use Multer as a small, bounded multipart parser at the application edge, then write the accepted bytes to a private object-storage key. For an education product, keep avatar objects and tenant backup snapshots in separate namespaces and apply different authorization rules. The simplest design is usually Multer memory storage for small avatars, a strict byte limit, content checks, a server-generated key, and a database record that points to the object. items.title: PHP Readies Critical Security Updates to Patch Another RCE Flaw
items.summary: PHP has released security updates addressing seven critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities across its supported versions, just four weeks after patches for the widely exploited PHP2Shell flaws. SecurityWeek reports: One of the security defects expected to be resolved is CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution (RCE) defect in the file-upload progress tracking functionality. The vulnerability was publicly disclosed two days after PHP2Shell made headlines. PHP's maintainers warned at the time that the security flaw can be triggered only under an unusual combination of configuration and code. "An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled," PHP said last month. Noting that patches would be released as part of the regular update cycle, PHP developers recommended disabling session upload, a setting also listed as a mitigation for CVE-2026-109619, one of the two RCE bugs tracked as PHP2Shell. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

Use cron for the first problem and an at-least-once queue for the second. A single delayed queue job is reasonable when the deadline is no more than seven days away; for longer horizons, run a periodic selector that enqueues only reminders entering the delivery window. The decisive invariant is not “the scheduler ran.” It is “one logical reminder produced at most one externally visible send, even when delivery was attempted more than once.” TL;DR: keep the business deadline in durable application data, let cron select due reminders, publish small jobs, and make the worker idempotent. Do not make a 900-second cron invocation carry a large batch, and do not treat a successful queue publish as proof that the customer received anything. Infrai is one concrete fit for that trigger-and-queue boundary: cron and queue capabilities sit behind one REST API and one credential, and its public discovery response exposes the current method, path, and JSON Schema before integration. items.title: How to add a working contact form to Next.js without an API route
items.summary: Every Next.js site eventually needs a contact form. And every time, the same question comes up: where do the submissions actually go? Next.js on Vercel or Netlify has no mail server. So you either write some backend code, configure an email provider, or hand the job to a service. Let's look at the three options, then build the simplest one step by step. Create app/api/contact/route.js, validate the input, and send an email with a provider like Resend, Postmark or SendGrid. Pros: full control, no third party for the form itself. Cons: you own everything: domain verification (SPF/DKIM), spam protection, rate limiting, storing submissions, and keeping it working when something changes. For a simple portfolio or client site, that's a lot of moving parts. Netlify Forms works well if you're on Netlify, but it ties your form to that host. Move to Vercel or a VPS and you rewrite it. You point the form at an external endpoint that receives the submission, filters spam and notifies you. No backend code, and it works on any host. This is what we'll build. Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps. items.title: Palo Alto Networks Signs $4.5 Billion Deal For Applied Compute
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has agreed to acquire AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion as it expands beyond traditional cybersecurity into securing enterprise AI systems, including the training and deployment of open-weight models. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Reuters reports: Palo Alto Networks has been repositioning itself as an integrated cybersecurity provider, with recent deals, including its $3.35 billion acquisition of cloud management and monitoring firm Chronosphere and an agreement with Israeli startup Koi. The company is looking to tap growing cybersecurity spending as the rapid adoption of AI creates new security risks and gives attackers new ways to exploit vulnerabilities. "AI tools are surfacing vulnerabilities faster than companies can patch them, and that is pushing customers to consolidate onto fewer platforms," said Catharine Trebnick, senior research analyst at Rosenblatt Securities. With the acquisition of Applied Compute, Palo Alto aims to offer a technology platform that helps customers securely train and deploy open-weight models as they expand their use of AI. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

Both publish official agent skills, and the main skill of each has about 850,000 installs or more. It is tempting to start with the rendering model. I would start with the license, because for many teams it settles the question before any code runs. HyperFrames ships under Apache 2.0, so any company can use it commercially. Remotion is free for individuals, non-profits and for-profit companies with up to 3 employees; everyone else needs a paid Company License. If you are a React team that fits the free tier or will pay for a Company License, Remotion is a strong fit. items.summary: At 100% display scaling, our Windows app had a red icon in its title bar. We closed it, switched to 200% and launched the same executable. The icon turned blue. Both colors came from the same ICO file. We had given each image inside it a different color so we could answer a practical question: when a window icon looks blurry, which image should you open in your editor? We used a square with a white mark in the corner. The 16 × 16 version is red, the 24 × 24 version is orange and the 32 × 32 version is blue. Each of the five larger sizes has its own color, too. items.title: TypeScript `Const` Assertions on Function Arguments in 2026: When Inline `as const` Beats a Generic Constraint
items.summary: TypeScript Const Assertions on Function Arguments in 2026: When Inline as const Beats a Generic Constraint This article was written with the assistance of AI, under human supervision and review. Developers preserve literal types by adding generic constraints to function signatures. This forces every caller to satisfy the constraint, even when the function does not need narrower types. The function signature grows complex, and callers lose flexibility. When a route definition function demands a constraint like T extends readonly string[], teams must decide whether that constraint belongs in the signature or at the call site. TypeScript 3.4 introduced const assertions with as const syntax (documented in the TypeScript 3.4 release notes), allowing developers to freeze literal types at the expression level. When applied inline to function arguments, as const narrows the type at the call site without changing the function signature. The function accepts the widened type, but the caller supplies a narrowed literal that TypeScript preserves through inference. This pattern shifts type narrowing from the function's responsibility to the caller's control. The function signature stays simple.

items.title: Anthropic Tops $2 Trillion Market Cap After IPO Debut
items.summary: Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut Thursday in the largest initial public offering in history. Shares opened at $111.50, a 34% premium that briefly pushed the Claude developer's market capitalization above $2 trillion, making it one of the world's most valuable companies. CNBC reports: The 5-year-old company captivated the corporate world with its Claude AI models and products, which have fueled its meteoric rise this year. Anthropic said in its prospectus that it generated $33.24 billion in revenue for the nine months ended Sept. 30, up a staggering 1,200% from the same period last year. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI, now its chief rival. Anthropic has faced a sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, including by President Donald Trump and other senior government officials. [The Pentagon formally designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk in March following a dispute over military use of its AI models.] Read more of this story at Slashdot.

items.title: Launch HN: Onlook (YC W25) – An open-source developer tool for designers
items.summary: Hey HN, I'm Daniel, founder of Onlook (https://github.com/onlook-dev/onlook and onlook.com). Onlook is a desktop app that puts a canvas on top of your real codebase, letting you design directly in code with the agent you already use. Over 25,000 designers and developers have supported the project, 100+ have contributed, and it's been the #1 trending repo in the world twice. We just rebuilt the entire product as an agentic design tool, and open-sourced it to the community. Here’s a demo video: (https://youtu.be/BogcYWf4siM) If you're an engineer, traditional engineering tools are largely built for convergence, whereas designers tend to explore and diverge on ideas. Onlook gives designers a familiar canvas while managing all of the dev processes that get between them and making mind-blowing designs in code. Designers can work on a multiple simultaneous worktrees that run on the real app locally, and every change lands as a PR you can review or throw away, so there aren’t mockups to rebuild. items.title: The Rive Handoff Checklist: 10 Things Developers and Animators Should Agree On Before the First Keyframe
items.summary: Rive is great at one thing Lottie and video can't do: the animation reacts. A button knows it's hovered, a mascot knows the user got the answer wrong, a progress ring knows it's at 73%. But that power comes with a catch. A Rive file is not just artwork anymore. It's a small piece of your app's logic, and it has an API. And like any API, it breaks when the two sides didn't agree on the contract first. After 10+ years in motion design and a lot of Rive projects for product teams, I've noticed the same thing again and again: almost every "the animation doesn't work" message I get is not a bug. It's a missing agreement. So here's the checklist I go through with developers before I start animating. Steal it for your next project. 1. State machine name Your code loads the state machine by its exact name. State Machine 1 (the default) works, but it's easy to rename later and silently break everything. Agree on one clear name early, for example Mascot SM or Button SM, and don't change it without telling each other. 2. Input names and types This is the big one. items.summary: joshuark quotes a report from BleepingComputer: Microsoft is testing a new feature that lets enterprise IT administrators remotely lock stolen or lost Windows devices without wiping them. Named Remote Lock, this new feature is shipping to devices upgraded to Windows 11 Insider Preview builds in the Beta (Build 26320.10003) and Experimental (Build 26340.10013) channels. Admins can use Microsoft Intune custom configuration profiles to lock Microsoft Entra-joined, hybrid-joined, or MDM-enrolled devices that run Windows Enterprise, Education, or Pro. After the IT department remotely locks the device, the system can only be unlocked via Intune, since PINs, passwords, local admins, or web sign-ins will no longer work. Microsoft added that the user's credentials will remain valid and can still be used to sign into other devices that haven't been locked. "Windows signs out every active session, hides all sign-in options and shows a locked screen," said Windows Insider communications lead Stephen Lines. items.title: Make the agent use the existing Link component, not a raw , for internal routes
items.summary: The agent adds a “Back to settings” control as . The app already has a Link (or RouterLink, or Next.js Link) that prefetches, keeps the client transition, and applies the active class from the design system. The raw anchor does a full reload, loses draft state on the page, and looks unstyled for a frame. I’ve started treating a raw to an internal path as a merge question, not as a finished navigation change. External URLs, mailto:, and file downloads can stay anchors. In-app paths should go through the shared component. The model has seen millions of HTML examples. href="/settings" looks correct, and it will work in the preview. What it will not do is honor the app’s scroll restoration, locale prefix, base path, or analytics hook that lives on Link. A new tab target also disappears: the shared component may already set it, or may explicitly forbid it for internal routes. A full reload on an internal click is easy to miss in a happy-path click-through and expensive in a form or a wizard. Internal paths use the shared Link External URLs use (or the shared ExternalLink if you have one), with rel set the way the app already sets it Do not invent a second wrapper to “add prefetch” Hash

items.title: Building a Cross-Platform UI SDK in .NET 10: C# to JavaScript Without WASM, and GPU Pixels Without a WebView
items.summary: If you are a .NET developer building products across web, mobile, and desktop, you usually have to pick your trade-off: Maintain separate stacks: C# on the backend, React or TypeScript on the web, and Swift, Kotlin, or Dart for mobile. Blazor WASM: stay in C#, but ship the .NET runtime to the browser and pay for it in the first download. WebView wrappers: share UI code across desktop and mobile, but give up native rendering and the platform's feel. Since January, I have been building eQuantic.UI, an open-source UI SDK for .NET 10 designed to remove these trade-offs. The idea is simple: write your components once, in strongly typed C#, against a declarative visual vocabulary, and let the SDK realize each target through its own real rendering path. One C# codebase. Real web. Real native. You can try it right now in the browser playground: write a component, press Run, and watch it render, with nothing to install. The source is on GitHub. In eQuantic.UI, there is no Razor, no XAML, no HTML templates, and no CSS files. items.title: What three months of shipping an AlarmKit app taught me
items.summary: In late August we shipped a small iOS 26 app that turns calendar events into AlarmKit alarms: if an event title contains a keyword you registered, a real alarm rings some minutes before it, through Silent mode and Focus, until you stop it. I wrote up the launch-week lessons back then. This post is the other half: things that only showed up after real people had been using it for a few months. None of them are in the docs, and one of them came from a user report that ended with "I had to restart my phone". AlarmPresentation.Alert takes LocalizedStringResource values for the title and buttons. It is tempting to pass keys and let the system localize them. The full-screen alert is rendered by a system process, not by your app. When that process resolves a LocalizedStringResource, "the main bundle" is not your app. In our case the alarm came up showing the raw key — in our project the source language is Japanese, so English users saw Japanese. Other developers have reported the same thing after a device restart (FB20472264 on the Apple Developer Forums). items.title: Background processing in .NET 8 with BackgroundService and Channel
items.summary: This post was originally published in Portuguese on my blog: Processando em segundo plano no .NET 8 com BackgroundService e Channel. We've all been there: the endpoint receives a request, does something slow (generates a report, sends an email, calls a slow service) and the client sits waiting until it times out. The classic way out is to respond right away and do the work in the background. You can jump straight to a broker like RabbitMQ, but that's often overkill. In .NET 8 you already have what you need at home: BackgroundService and Channel . The API doesn't process anything. It registers the job, puts it in a queue and returns 202 Accepted with a Location header. On the other side, a BackgroundService loops reading from the queue and processing one job at a time. The client polls GET /jobs/{id} to get the status: Queued, Processing, Completed or Failed. The project has three pieces: ChannelJobQueue (the queue), JobStore (a concurrent dictionary with the state of each job) and JobWorker (the consumer). items.title: Parents: please don’t buy Grand Theft Auto VI for your child
items.summary: Rockstar Games’ brilliant 18-rated criminal caper is stuffed with sex, drugs and violence. It is the most explicit game I’ve ever played – and it really is not for kids I am haunted still by an interaction I had at my stepson’s ninth birthday party in 2014, where one of the kids asked if I could put on Grand Theft Auto V for them all. “I have it at home!”, he said, giving me the puppy-dog eyes. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “no way”. items.title: How to Generate an APNs JWT Provider Token From a .p8 Key
items.summary: Originally published at https://bestlatestapps.com/blog/how-to-generate-an-apns-jwt-provider-token-from-a-p8-key/. Token-based push authentication is simpler than certificates once it works. Getting it to work the first time, though, usually involves a 403 InvalidProviderToken with no further explanation. APNs JWT generator builds and signs a correct token from your .p8 key, Key ID and Team ID, decodes it, counts down to expiry, and gives you a curl command to test against APNs. An APNs provider token is a JWT: Header: {"alg": "ES256", "kid": " "} Claims: {"iss": " ", "iat": } Each part is base64url-encoded without padding, joined with a dot, and signed using ECDSA on the P-256 curve with SHA-256. The base64url signature becomes the third part. The page does the signing with the browser's Web Crypto API and shows the decoded header and claims next to the result. Key ID: in Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles → Keys, and in the file name AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8 (the page reads it from the name when it can). items.title: macOS 27 quietly renamed the screenshot location key
items.summary: I'm Bazi, and I make Pizazoo, a screenshot organizer for Mac, iPhone and iPad. Pizazoo doesn't take screenshots. On the Mac it organizes the ones you take with Shift-Command-3, 4 or 5 (or apps like CleanShot X, Shottr and Xnapper) by watching the folders they save to. So "where does macOS save screenshots?" is a question my app has to answer correctly, and in Settings the System Screenshots row has a Change Location… button that changes the answer. On macOS 27 that button stopped working. You picked a folder, the app wrote the setting, restarted SystemUIServer like it always had, and the next screenshot saved exactly where it did before. On a Mac where nothing had set the new key, that meant the Desktop. No error, no failed write. The setting simply had no effect. The Terminal tip that most guides give, defaults write com.apple.screencapture location followed by killall SystemUIServer, has the same problem. On macOS 27 it runs cleanly and changes nothing. items.title: Validating a High-Performance Cloud Object Store with Lightweight Formal Methods
items.summary: Abstract: We report on our experience validating S3 Express One Zone, a high-performance Amazon S3 storage class launched in November 2023. We focused on its distributed metadata index, which implements a hierarchical namespace using distributed transactions. We check strong consistency and durability under crashes, network delays, and timeouts. Building on our prior work on lightweight formal methods, we combined executable reference models with property-based testing and stateless model checking. Applying these techniques to a production distributed system required three new techniques: a white-box approach to checking serializability; compositional validation of the data and control planes; and long-running canaries that use reference models to check correctness across deployments. We extended Shuttle, our open-source stateless checker, to support a production async Rust runtime and failure injection, including cancelled operations and timeouts. Our main finding is that this approach is sustainable at engineering scale. GPU Watch keeps SSH connectivity, GPU query results, and data freshness separate. Monitor multiple hosts over SSH No agent installed on remote servers Uses your existing SSH config and keys Tracks physical GPUs by UUID No backend, telemetry, or third-party dependencies Written in Swift/SwiftUI, open source under GPLv3 It's currently available as a source build for macOS. items.summary: An anonymous reader quotes a report from 404 Media: A new study from Gallup looked at how young people across the world are making friends, both digitally and in person. The good news is that around 93% of the young people surveyed reported having at least one strong in-person friendship. The weird news is that 33% said they had an AI companion. Gallup's study is lengthy and nuanced. It partnered with the Boston Children's Digital Wellness Lab to conduct the study and used online surveys of more than 16,000 young people from the ages of 15 to 22 in 16 different countries. A lot of the topline results won't surprise anyone living in today's constantly online digital-forward age. Gallup found that respondents felt their in-person friendships were their strongest, that digital friendships complemented rather than replaced in-person ones, and that stronger friendships made people happier no matter how the connection was made. Three things that stood out were how the young respondents talked about AI, loneliness, and doomscrolling. items.title: Switching LLMs mid-conversation is a ski-rental problem (30 minute read)

items.title: 'Java4Shell' Flaw Exposes OpenJDK to RCE via Base64
items.summary: Longtime Slashdot reader HnT writes: Security researchers at Calif have disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a critical 9.2-rated memory-corruption bug in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 decoder. By sending a malformed string ending in a stray = character, attackers can trigger an out-of-bounds heap write to leak sensitive memory or achieve pre-auth remote code execution on major platforms like Jira, Jenkins, and Keycloak. Although Calif says the vulnerability is difficult to exploit, Oracle released a critical patch update Tuesday, and CISA urged organizations to update immediately. OpenJDK's security advisory can be found here. The Calif researchers warned that vulnerable systems could remain exposed for five to 10 years, given how slowly some organizations patch their infrastructure. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

items.title: A receipt that says "nothing was changed" has to be true
items.summary: Our Mac menu bar app has two buttons, Free Agent RAM and Stop Runaways. Each one runs a small Node.js script that finds agent processes eating memory or CPU, and stops them. When the script finishes, the app shows a receipt that lists what it did. If Node.js isn't installed, the script can't run. The app handles that: it shows "Couldn't free agent memory" and says what went wrong. Before the 1.2.10 release it also did something else first. It ran xcrun simctl shutdown all, which shuts down every simulator on the Mac. The order was the bug. In both button handlers, the call that shuts down simulators sat above the check for whether Node.js had run. A person without Node.js would click the button, see "Nothing was changed", and have every running simulator shut down anyway. The receipt was false. Nothing in the app could have told them otherwise, because the shutdown happened before the app looked at the result. The change was moving one line below the check. items.title: Eliminating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference with Integer-Only Arithmetic (15 minute read)
items.summary: A floating-point number stores a fixed number of significant digits and a separate exponent. When two numbers with very different exponents are added, the small one has to be shifted to line up with the big one, and the digits that fall off on the end are gone. That means that (a+b)+c is not always equal to a+(b+c). This post looks at what happens when integer addition, which is exact, is used.

items.title: What objective is reasoning solving? (12 minute read)
items.summary: Reasoning is pathfinding in token space. There are many paths from the problem to a correct answer, and the model traverses each of them with each sample. A path is not guaranteed to converge to the correct answer - it's only in aggregate, over the distribution of paths, do we get a high probability of success. RL training directly raises the success probability. The gains credited to 'thinking longer' come from the search paid for during training rather than at inference.

items.summary: Anthropic plans to start trading its shares by the end of next week. Investors anticipated a target valuation of around $1.5 trillion last week, but some major investors are now pushing for it to be lower. items.title: Fable 5.2 and Jagged AGI (18 minute read)
items.summary: AI models are likely to soon cross the boundary into Artificial General Intelligence. Claude Fable 5.2 is almost as good as most human experts at most intellectual tasks that can be completed with a computer. It still makes mistakes and requires human guidance, but it demonstrates impressive work in many tests. There are still important areas in many tasks where the model is jagged enough to fall well behind human capability, but it isn't about simple errors or hallucinations anymore.
